claims.text: The reroute was traffic-justified, so the driver's turn onto Upper Serangoon Road was a reaction to an incident on his own route and not a detour of his own choosing. EV-ADVIS-05005-01 is an LTA traffic-incident record for a VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway, the expressway the recommended route runs on (optimal_route_via: Punggol Central, TPE, KPE, Paya Lebar Road), with a validity window of 09:59:38 to 10:54:38 that covers the trip (10:14:38 to 10:38:08). POL-RD-23 requires only a traffic advisory that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window, and its admissible 'incident' vocabulary expressly includes BREAKDOWN and VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN. The rider's framing of the turn as an unexplained deviation is therefore wrong on the face of the record.

The driver told the rider, in the app, what he was doing and why, and the rider accepted it. MSG-05005-003 - 'Sorry ah, KPE got breakdown inside the tunnel so I go Upper Serangoon Road instead' - was sent at 10:24:30, delivered, and read by the rider, who answered 'ok noted' at 10:25:00 (MSG-05005-004). POL-RD-21 accepts in-app chat as the channel for this notice, requires only that the driver give 'a brief reason', and expressly provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment 'the deviation is agreed'. This log confirms it. The rider raised nothing at the time and nothing during the thirteen minutes of trip that remained after his reply; his assertion that he 'had no say' is contradicted by his own reply in the same log.

With the reroute traffic-justified under POL-RD-23 and the rider's acknowledgment confirmed in the chat log under POL-RD-21 - which makes the deviation an agreed one - the row that fits this case is POL-RD-24(a), and no refund is due. The deviation exceeds the 1.0 km tolerance (1.70 km), so rows (c) and (e) are unavailable, and the driver was not silent: he gave the rider the reason for the reroute and the rider accepted it, which is the opposite of the uninformed-rider rows (b) and (d). The metered fare of 23.04 SGD should stand and the ruling should be NO_ACTION.

The deviation must be measured the way POL-RD-22 requires, on the platform's recorded distances - 13.8 km actual minus 12.1 km recommended = 1.70 km - and not on the GPS trace, which POL-RD-22 says is used only to show which route was taken and when and is never used to re-measure distance because a sparse trace understates a route's length. The driver does not dispute the 1.70 km figure; he asks only that the same measure, and no other, be applied to him, as the clause requires.

On POL-RD-24's own arithmetic the rider cannot reach the 5.00 SGD he asks. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 1.70 km x 0.92 SGD = 1.56 SGD. The two rows that can apply on a 1.70 km deviation where the rider is not treated as having agreed - row (b) and row (d) - both pay that same single figure and nothing else; no row of the matrix returns the whole 5.00 SGD, and none touches the base, time or platform components of the fare. A refund of 5.00 SGD would over-compensate the rider by 3.44 SGD, and the rider's round $5 figure is a number he has picked, not the excess distance fare the policy provides.

The charge the rider is contesting is an ordinary metered fare, not a route-based surcharge: base 3.80 + distance 12.70 + time 5.64 + platform fee 0.90 = 23.04 SGD, with no surge (multiplier 1.0), no ERP and no waiting fee, and the fare was finalised at 10:38:14 on trip completion. The only component attributable to the extra 1.70 km is the 1.56 SGD distance increment, so even on the rider's best case the record supports no more than that single line and nothing in the remaining 21.48 SGD.

To both parties: the rider filed this dispute contesting 5.00 SGD of a metered fare of 23.04 SGD, and the rider is owed part of what was charged — 1.56 SGD — not the whole 5.00 SGD.

How the deviation is measured (both sides agree, and I accept it): POL-RD-22 fixes the distance as the platform's recorded figures, 13.8 km actual minus 12.1 km recommended = 1.70 km. That is over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so the within-tolerance rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 cannot apply. The 1.70 km is not disputed, and the GPS trace is used only to show which roads were taken (Upper Serangoon Road from 10:21:38, rejoin at 10:35:21), not to re-measure distance, exactly as POL-RD-22 directs.

Why the driver's 'no refund' case fails (POL-RD-21): POL-RD-21 permits a traffic reroute only if the driver informs the rider by in-app chat 'before or at the point of deviation.' The platform logged the deviation at 10:21:30; the driver's explaining message (MSG-05005-003, 'KPE got breakdown ... so I go Upper Serangoon Road instead') was sent at 10:24:30 — about three minutes after the turn. Notice after the turn is not notice before or at the deviation, so the rider was not informed within the meaning of POL-RD-21, and the rider's 'ok noted' at 10:25:00 answers a message that came too late. An acknowledgment of a turn already taken is not the (a)-row agreement to a deviation the rider could still refuse. The driver's statement that he informed the passenger 'before I changed route' is contradicted by the chat log's own timestamps.

Why the outcome is still a refund whichever way traffic justification goes (POL-RD-23, POL-RD-24): the LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05005-01) is a VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN on the KPE — an admissible 'incident' type under POL-RD-23 — with a validity window (09:59:38 to 10:54:38) that overlaps the trip. Whether or not it is treated as lying on the recommended route (its own record leaves that 'undetermined'), the outcome is the same: if traffic-justified, row (b) applies (traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km); if not, row (d) applies (not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km). Both rows return the excess distance fare, so the open route-intersection point is not outcome-determinative and no POL-GEN-26 escalation is needed to resolve it.

The sum awarded (POL-RD-24): the excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 1.70 km x 0.92 SGD = 1.564, rounded to 1.56 SGD. That is the only component of the 23.04 SGD fare attributable to the extra distance (base 3.80 + distance 12.70 + time 5.64 + platform fee 0.90, no surge, no ERP, no waiting fee). No row of the matrix returns the whole fare, and nothing touches the base, time or platform lines, so the rider's round 5.00 SGD figure over-states the entitlement by 3.44 SGD. Since the rider filed and is owed part of the contested charge, the result is PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.56 SGD, and driver_compensation_sgd is null.

Confidence and forum (POL-GEN-22, POL-RD-25): the amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so no elevated threshold applies; POL-RD-25 sets the route-deviation bar at 0.80, POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off and the 1.70 km deviation is under 2 km in any event, and every artifact I relied on — trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare breakdown, traffic advisory — is COMPLETE at weight 1.0. My confidence is 0.85. No clause in this version produces a referral on a route deviation.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: I have decided this on the record. The rider is owed part of what was asked, so the ruling is a partial refund of 1.56 SGD.

THE NUMBERS ARE NOT IN DISPUTE. The metered fare charged was 23.04 SGD on a recorded 13.8 km against a recommended 12.1 km, so the deviation is 1.70 km measured the way POL-RD-22 requires - the platform's recorded distances, not the GPS trace, which the clause uses only to show which road was taken and when. Either way the trace confirms the routing: the vehicle is on Upper Serangoon Road from the 10:21:38 fix and only rejoins the recommended line at Paya Lebar Road from about 10:35. The driver is right that 1.70 km is the measure, and the rider is right that 1.70 km is above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so the within-tolerance rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 cannot apply.

WHY THIS IS NOT A NO-REFUND CASE. The driver's reroute is well explained. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05005-01 records a vehicle breakdown on the KPE (towards ECP) valid 09:59:38 to 10:54:38, which overlaps the trip window, and VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN is one of the incident types POL-RD-23 admits; so the turn was at least arguably traffic-justified and not a detour of the driver's own choosing. But the driver's further point - that he told the rider in time and she agreed, so row (a) of POL-RD-24 applies and nothing is refunded - is not supported. POL-RD-21 requires the notice, by in-app chat, before or at the point of deviation. The deviation was logged at 10:21:30 and the trace puts the vehicle on the non-recommended road from 10:21:38, but the driver's message MSG-05005-003 was sent at 10:24:30, roughly three minutes after the turn was taken, and the rider's reply 'ok noted' (MSG-05005-004) came at 10:25:00. The driver's counterparty statement that he informed the rider 'before I changed route' is contradicted by his own chat log. A late notice is not the notice POL-RD-21 requires, and an acknowledgment of a turn already taken is not the 'agreed' deviation row (a) needs - reading it otherwise would empty the 'before or at the point of deviation' requirement of meaning. The rider's account that the driver messaged only after turning off is the version the timestamps support.

WHAT FOLLOWS. With the deviation over 1 km and the rider not informed as POL-RD-21 requires, the case falls in POL-RD-24's refund rows, not row (a): row (b) if the reroute is traffic-justified and row (d) if it is not, and both refund the same sum, the excess distance fare. The record leaves one thing open - whether the LTA advisory lies on the recommended route, which its own note marks 'undetermined' - but this does not matter, because both candidate rows pay the same figure, so no POL-GEN-26 escalation is needed and that open point changes nothing.

THE AMOUNT. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge (POL-RD-24): 1.70 km x 0.92 SGD = 1.564 SGD, rounded to 1.56 SGD. Both parties are right that no row of the matrix returns the full 5.00 SGD asked; the rider's round figure is not the policy measure, and the base, time and platform components of the 23.04 SGD fare are not attributable to the extra 1.70 km. The rider is therefore owed 1.56 SGD, refunded against the 23.04 SGD metered fare, which stands CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.0.

CONFIDENCE AND WHO DECIDES. The amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so the AI ruling is final; POL-RD-25 sets the bar at 0.80 confidence and mine is 0.90. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact - the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log and the fare breakdown - is COMPLETE at weight 1.0. POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not applied (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false) and the 1.70 km deviation is under it in any event. No referral clause exists for a route deviation in this version, so there are none.

The GPS trace independently shows which route was taken, as POL-RD-22 uses it: the vehicle runs on Upper Serangoon Road from the 10:21:38 fix, on Upper Paya Lebar Road from 10:28:38, and only reaches Paya Lebar Road at 10:35:38, so the vehicle did leave the recommended TPE-KPE line and did not rejoin the recommended route until 10:35:21.

The driver gave the notice too late to satisfy POL-RD-21: the deviation is logged at 10:21:30 and the trace puts the vehicle on the non-recommended road from 10:21:38, but the driver's explaining message (MSG-05005-003) was sent at 10:24:30 - roughly three minutes after the point of deviation - while POL-RD-21 requires the rider to be informed by in-app chat before or at that point.

The driver's counterparty statement that he 'informed the passenger before I changed route' is contradicted by the chat log's own timestamps: the only message describing the reroute is MSG-05005-003 at 10:24:30, which is after the 10:21:30 deviation, so timely notice is not established on the driver's own account either.

The rider's reply 'ok noted' (MSG-05005-004, sent 10:25:00) cannot move this case into row (a) of POL-RD-24: it answers a notice that POL-RD-21 says had to come before or at the point of deviation, so the rider was never 'informed' within the meaning of that row, and an after-the-fact acknowledgment of a turn already taken is not agreement to a deviation she had no chance to refuse.

Even taking the traffic advisory at its highest, the case is row (b) of POL-RD-24 - traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km - and row (b) refunds the excess distance fare: the advisory is a VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN, an admissible incident type under POL-RD-23, and it overlaps the trip window (valid 09:59:38 to 10:54:38).

If the advisory is instead not treated as lying on the recommended route, the case is row (d) of POL-RD-24 - not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km - which refunds the excess distance fare in full; rows (b) and (d) pay the same sum, so the one fact the advisory itself leaves open (whether it intersects the recommended route, its own 'undetermined' note) is not outcome-determinative and no POL-GEN-26 escalation is needed to resolve it.

The sum to be returned is the excess distance fare under POL-RD-24: 1.70 km times the per_km_rate_sgd of 0.92 equals 1.564 SGD, rounded to 1.56 SGD, with no surge applied; that is the policy measure of the refund and it should be awarded to the rider.

The rider is carrying the disputed charge today: the metered fare was charged at 23.04 SGD with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION outcome would simply preserve that charge against the rider - only a refund moves it off the rider.

The reroute was traffic-justified, so the driver's turn onto Upper Serangoon Road was a reaction to an incident on his own route and not a detour of his own choosing. EV-ADVIS-05005-01 is an LTA traffic-incident record for a VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway, the expressway the recommended route runs on (optimal_route_via: Punggol Central, TPE, KPE, Paya Lebar Road), with a validity window of 09:59:38 to 10:54:38 that covers the trip (10:14:38 to 10:38:08). POL-RD-23 requires only a traffic advisory that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window, and its admissible 'incident' vocabulary expressly includes BREAKDOWN and VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN. The rider's framing of the turn as an unexplained deviation is therefore wrong on the face of the record.

The driver told the rider, in the app, what he was doing and why, and the rider accepted it. MSG-05005-003 - 'Sorry ah, KPE got breakdown inside the tunnel so I go Upper Serangoon Road instead' - was sent at 10:24:30, delivered, and read by the rider, who answered 'ok noted' at 10:25:00 (MSG-05005-004). POL-RD-21 accepts in-app chat as the channel for this notice, requires only that the driver give 'a brief reason', and expressly provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment 'the deviation is agreed'. This log confirms it. The rider raised nothing at the time and nothing during the thirteen minutes of trip that remained after his reply; his assertion that he 'had no say' is contradicted by his own reply in the same log.

With the reroute traffic-justified under POL-RD-23 and the rider's acknowledgment confirmed in the chat log under POL-RD-21 - which makes the deviation an agreed one - the row that fits this case is POL-RD-24(a), and no refund is due. The deviation exceeds the 1.0 km tolerance (1.70 km), so rows (c) and (e) are unavailable, and the driver was not silent: he gave the rider the reason for the reroute and the rider accepted it, which is the opposite of the uninformed-rider rows (b) and (d). The metered fare of 23.04 SGD should stand and the ruling should be NO_ACTION.

The deviation must be measured the way POL-RD-22 requires, on the platform's recorded distances - 13.8 km actual minus 12.1 km recommended = 1.70 km - and not on the GPS trace, which POL-RD-22 says is used only to show which route was taken and when and is never used to re-measure distance because a sparse trace understates a route's length. The driver does not dispute the 1.70 km figure; he asks only that the same measure, and no other, be applied to him, as the clause requires.

On POL-RD-24's own arithmetic the rider cannot reach the 5.00 SGD he asks. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 1.70 km x 0.92 SGD = 1.56 SGD. The two rows that can apply on a 1.70 km deviation where the rider is not treated as having agreed - row (b) and row (d) - both pay that same single figure and nothing else; no row of the matrix returns the whole 5.00 SGD, and none touches the base, time or platform components of the fare. A refund of 5.00 SGD would over-compensate the rider by 3.44 SGD, and the rider's round $5 figure is a number he has picked, not the excess distance fare the policy provides.

The charge the rider is contesting is an ordinary metered fare, not a route-based surcharge: base 3.80 + distance 12.70 + time 5.64 + platform fee 0.90 = 23.04 SGD, with no surge (multiplier 1.0), no ERP and no waiting fee, and the fare was finalised at 10:38:14 on trip completion. The only component attributable to the extra 1.70 km is the 1.56 SGD distance increment, so even on the rider's best case the record supports no more than that single line and nothing in the remaining 21.48 SGD.
